title.es: Voz narrativa y punto de vista

es: Reconocer la voz narrativa (primera persona, tercera limitada u omnisciente) en fragmentos breves y justificarla con una pista.

teaching.en: I open the letter and my hands tremble.
teaching.es: Abro la carta y me tiemblan las manos.
teaching.explanationEs: El pronombre I es la pista de la primera persona: el narrador es un personaje y solo cuenta lo que vive y siente.
segments: I open the letter
and my hands tremble.
teaching.audioText: I open the letter and my hands tremble.

teaching.en: Mara opens the letter and wonders why her father has written.
teaching.es: Mara abre la carta y se pregunta por qué ha escrito su padre.
teaching.explanationEs: Tercera persona limitada: el narrador sigue a Mara y conocemos solo sus pensamientos.
segments: Mara opens the letter and wonders
why her father has written.
teaching.audioText: Mara opens the letter and wonders why her father has written.

teaching.en: The narrator tells us what Mara fears and what her father hides.
teaching.es: El narrador nos cuenta lo que teme Mara y lo que oculta su padre.
teaching.explanationEs: Aquí el narrador entra en dos mentes a la vez: es omnisciente.
segments: The narrator tells us what Mara
fears and what her father hides.
teaching.audioText: The narrator tells us what Mara fears and what her father hides.

teaching.en: A limited narrator shows one mind, but an omniscient narrator shows many.
teaching.es: Un narrador limitado muestra una sola mente, pero uno omnisciente muestra muchas.
teaching.explanationEs: Limited y omniscient se distinguen por cuántas mentes abre el narrador.
segments: A limited narrator shows one mind,
but an omniscient narrator shows many.
teaching.audioText: A limited narrator shows one mind, but an omniscient narrator shows many.

teaching.en: One clue is the pronoun: I points to first person, and she or he points to third person.
teaching.es: Una pista es el pronombre: I indica primera persona, y she o he indican tercera persona.
teaching.explanationEs: Un pronombre no basta: primero mira la persona (I / she) y luego cuántas mentes se abren.
segments: One clue is the pronoun: I points to first
person, and she or he points to third person.
teaching.audioText: One clue is the pronoun: I points to first person, and she or he points to third person.

teaching.en: Readers wonder whose voice they hear when the narrator never says I.
teaching.es: Los lectores se preguntan de quién es la voz que oyen cuando el narrador nunca dice yo.
teaching.explanationEs: La voz narrativa es el tono y el punto de vista de quien cuenta, aunque no diga I.
segments: Readers wonder whose voice they hear
when the narrator never says I.
teaching.audioText: Readers wonder whose voice they hear when the narrator never says I.

prompt.es: Elige el tipo de narrador del fragmento según lo que cuenta.

choices.text: The narrator is a character who says I.
The narrator follows one character's thoughts.
The narrator knows the thoughts of many characters.

feedback.es: El pronombre I muestra que quien cuenta es un personaje de la historia.

hint.es: Busca el pronombre con el que habla el narrador.

origin.text: I opened the door and felt my heart beating fast.

prompt.es: Completa: «Este narrador sabe lo que piensa cada personaje, así que es omnisciente.»

feedback.es: Un narrador que conoce los pensamientos de todos los personajes tiene un punto de vista omnisciente.

origin.text: This narrator knows what every character thinks, so the view is ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El narrador nos cuenta lo que siente Mara.»

answer.text: The narrator tells us what Mara feels

feedback.es: Tell va directamente con us, y what Mara feels mantiene el orden de una frase afirmativa.

hint.es: El verbo tell va con us sin preposición.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fragmento con el tipo de narrador.

pairs: My hands shake as I read it.
Sara reads it and wonders if he lied.
Sara fears the truth, and Leo hides it.

feedback.es: El pronombre I marca la primera persona; una sola mente, tercera limitada; dos mentes, omnisciente.

pairs: My hands shake as I read it.
Sara reads it and wonders if he lied.
Sara fears the truth, and Leo hides it.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige la pista que muestra quién cuenta.

choices.text: The narrator follows a friend.
The narrator speaks about himself.
The narrator knows everyone's thoughts.

feedback.es: El narrador dice I y habla de sus propias piernas y dudas: es un personaje que cuenta su historia.

origin.audio: I walked home alone. My legs were heavy, and I did not know what to say to her.

prompt.es: Completa: «La voz del cuento suena joven.»

feedback.es: La voz narrativa es el tono con que habla el narrador: aquí suena joven.

origin.text: The ___ of the story sounds young.

prompt.es: Elige qué tipo de narrador hay en el fragmento de Tom y Ana.

choices.text: The narrator stays in Tom's mind only.
Tom himself is telling the story.
The narrator enters the minds of two characters.

feedback.es: El narrador cuenta lo que piensa Tom y también lo que piensa Ana: entra en dos mentes.

origin.text: Tom looked at the clock. He wondered if Ana was angry. Across the room, Ana wondered the same about him.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige de qué mente nos habla el narrador.

choices.text: Only Mara's mind.
Mara's and her brother's minds.
Only the brother's mind.

feedback.es: Todo lo que sabemos lo sabe Mara: sus preguntas y su certeza; no entramos en la mente de su hermano.

origin.audio: Mara was standing at the window. Why had her brother not called? She was sure he was angry with her.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una pista es el pronombre: I señala la primera persona.»

feedback.es: Clue significa pista: el pronombre ayuda a reconocer quién cuenta la historia.

origin.text: One ___ is the pronoun: I points to first person.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los lectores se preguntan qué quiere su padre de ella.»

answer.text: Readers wonder what her father wants from her

feedback.es: Después de wonder, la pregunta indirecta mantiene el orden afirmativo: what her father wants.

prompt.es: Elige el tipo de narrador del fragmento del lago.

choices.text: The narrator knows the thoughts of everyone at the lake.
A character tells the story and says I.
The narrator follows only the thoughts of one friend called Sam.

feedback.es: We y I muestran que alguien del grupo cuenta la historia: es una voz de primera persona.

origin.text: We walked to the lake, and I felt proud of us.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dato muestra que el narrador entra en más de una mente.

choices.text: Leo's hope for a gift.
The smell of the kitchen.
What the mother knows about the box.

feedback.es: Leo no sabe lo que hay en la caja, pero el narrador sí sabe lo que sabe la madre: entra en dos mentes.

origin.audio: Leo opened the box. He hoped it was a gift. His mother, in the kitchen, knew it was only old books and smiled.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sus manos tiemblan cuando abre la carta.»

feedback.es: Hands es plural, así que el verbo va sin -s: tremble.

origin.text: Her hands ___ when she opens the letter.

es: Reconocer el estilo indirecto libre y separar la voz del narrador de los pensamientos del personaje.

teaching.en: Mara looked at the clock. Was he really going to be late again?
teaching.es: Mara miró el reloj. ¿De verdad iba a llegar tarde otra vez?
teaching.explanationEs: La pregunta directa dentro de la narración en pasado es la voz de Mara: no hay «she asked herself».
segments: Mara looked at the clock. Was he
really going to be late again?
teaching.audioText: Mara looked at the clock. Was he really going to be late again?

teaching.en: He would surely come tomorrow. Of course he would!
teaching.es: Seguro que vendría mañana. ¡Claro que vendría!
teaching.explanationEs: Tomorrow en un relato en pasado es marca de estilo libre: el narrador diría the next day.
segments: He would surely come tomorrow.
Of course he would!
teaching.audioText: He would surely come tomorrow. Of course he would!

teaching.en: She stopped at the door. What a silly idea this was!
teaching.es: Se paró en la puerta. ¡Qué idea tan tonta era esta!
teaching.explanationEs: What a + exclamación es la voz de ella; this (y no that) acerca el texto a su mente.
segments: She stopped at the door. What
a silly idea this was!
teaching.audioText: She stopped at the door. What a silly idea this was!

teaching.en: She had no doubt about it: he was coming, and nothing could stop him now.
teaching.es: No tenía ninguna duda: él venía y nada podía detenerlo ahora.
teaching.explanationEs: Now dentro de un relato en pasado muestra el punto de vista del personaje, no el del narrador.
segments: She had no doubt about it: he was
coming, and nothing could stop him now.
teaching.audioText: She had no doubt about it: he was coming, and nothing could stop him now.

teaching.en: She felt nervous, and her mind went back to that day. Was it really her fault?
teaching.es: Se sentía nerviosa y su mente volvió a aquel día. ¿De verdad era culpa suya?
teaching.explanationEs: Primero narración (felt nervous) y luego pensamiento en forma de pregunta directa, en pasado.
segments: She felt nervous, and her mind went back
to that day. Was it really her fault?
teaching.audioText: She felt nervous, and her mind went back to that day. Was it really her fault?

teaching.en: Mara thought that he would be late again. He would be late again!
teaching.es: Mara pensó que él llegaría tarde otra vez. ¡Llegaría tarde otra vez!
teaching.explanationEs: La primera frase es estilo indirecto (thought that); la segunda es estilo libre: sin verbo de pensar y con exclamación.
segments: Mara thought that he would be late
again. He would be late again!
teaching.audioText: Mara thought that he would be late again. He would be late again!

prompt.es: Elige la frase que es el pensamiento de Leo, sin verbo de pensar.

choices.text: Leo opened the fridge.
Was there no milk again?
He closed it and sat down.

feedback.es: La pregunta directa es lo que Leo piensa; las otras dos frases cuentan sus acciones.

hint.es: Busca la frase que es una pregunta en medio de la narración.

origin.text: Leo opened the fridge. Was there no milk again? He closed it and sat down.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ana esperó. ¡Seguro que vendría mañana!»

feedback.es: Surely marca la certeza del personaje: Ana está convencida, aunque el narrador siga en pasado.

origin.text: Ana waited. He would ___ come tomorrow!

prompt.es: Ordena: «¡Qué idea tan tonta era esta!»

answer.text: What a silly idea this was

feedback.es: What a + nombre expresa la emoción del personaje y was mantiene el pasado de la narración.

hint.es: Empieza con What a y termina con was.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su estilo.

pairs: Mara looked at the clock.
Mara believed that he would be late.
He would be late again!
"I am late," said Mara.

feedback.es: La narración cuenta hechos, el indirecto usa thought that, el libre pone la voz sin verbo y el directo usa comillas.

pairs: Mara looked at the clock.
Mara believed that he would be late.
He would be late again!
"I am late," said Mara.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué rasgo muestra que es el pensamiento de Tom.

choices.text: The verb to think before the sentence.
The pronoun I at the start.
Tomorrow in a past story, plus a strong feeling.

feedback.es: Tomorrow dentro de un relato en pasado y el sentimiento fuerte son marcas de la voz del personaje.

origin.audio: Tom smiled at the door. Tomorrow he would tell her everything. Of course he would!

prompt.es: Completa: «Mara pensó que él llegaría tarde.»

feedback.es: Thought that introduce el pensamiento de forma indirecta, con un verbo de pensar explícito.

origin.text: Mara ___ that he would be late.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que transmite la voz de Sam, no la del narrador.

choices.text: What a waste of time this was!
The train was late.
Sam put his bag down and waited.

feedback.es: What a… this was! es una exclamación del personaje; las otras dos frases narran hechos.

origin.text: The train was late. What a waste of time this was! Sam put his bag down and waited.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué frase es el pensamiento de Clara.

choices.text: The moment she opened the exam.
The question about why nobody warned her.
The way her pen moved.

feedback.es: La pregunta directa sin verbo de pensar es la voz de Clara; las otras dos cosas son acciones.

origin.audio: Clara opened her exam. Why had nobody told her it was so long? Her pen moved slowly.

prompt.es: Completa: «No tenía ninguna duda: él vendría.»

feedback.es: No doubt muestra la certeza del personaje, dentro de una frase narrada en pasado.

origin.text: She had no ___: he was coming.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿De verdad tenía que ir sola?»

answer.text: Did she really have to go alone

feedback.es: La pregunta directa conserva la inversión (Did she…?) y el pasado del narrador, sin verbo de pensar.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que pasa el pensamiento de Ana a estilo indirecto libre.

choices.text: Ana said, "The test is easy."
Ana felt sure that the test was easy.
The test would be easy, of course!

feedback.es: El estilo libre quita el verbo de pensar y mantiene el pasado (would), con una exclamación como voz de Ana.

origin.text: Ana waited outside the room. She felt sure about the test.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué frase suena como el pensamiento de Sam.

choices.text: The question about whether it is always like this.
The fact that the bus did not come.
The way Sam pulled his coat.

feedback.es: La pregunta directa es el pensamiento de Sam; las otras dos frases son hechos narrados.

origin.audio: The bus did not come. Was it always like this? Sam pulled his coat closer.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se sentía nerviosa, y su mente volvió a aquel día.»

feedback.es: Nervous describe el ánimo del personaje; a continuación su mente vuelve al pasado.

origin.text: She felt ___, and her mind went back to that day.

es: Comprender el estado de ánimo, el motivo y una expresión clave de un personaje a partir de sus acciones en un fragmento de cuento (texto y audio).

teaching.en: Mara feels anxious before the exam, so she tries to avoid her friends.
teaching.es: Mara se siente inquieta antes del examen, así que intenta evitar a sus amigos.
teaching.explanationEs: El ánimo (anxious) explica la acción (avoid): del motivo a la conducta.
segments: Mara feels anxious before the exam, so
she tries to avoid her friends.
teaching.audioText: Mara feels anxious before the exam, so she tries to avoid her friends.

teaching.en: Leo is eager to start, but his sister looks reluctant.
teaching.es: Leo tiene muchas ganas de empezar, pero su hermana parece reacia.
teaching.explanationEs: Eager y reluctant son opuestos: muchas ganas frente a poca gana de hacer algo.
segments: Leo is eager to start,
but his sister looks reluctant.
teaching.audioText: Leo is eager to start, but his sister looks reluctant.

teaching.en: When the door opened, Tom felt relieved: nobody had seen him.
teaching.es: Cuando se abrió la puerta, Tom se sintió aliviado: nadie lo había visto.
teaching.explanationEs: Relieved es el ánimo de quien deja de preocuparse; had seen sitúa el hecho antes del alivio.
segments: When the door opened, Tom felt
relieved: nobody had seen him.
teaching.audioText: When the door opened, Tom felt relieved: nobody had seen him.

teaching.en: She felt guilty because she had not called her grandmother.
teaching.es: Se sentía culpable porque no había llamado a su abuela.
teaching.explanationEs: Guilty + because da el motivo de la emoción con un hecho anterior (had not called).
segments: She felt guilty because she
had not called her grandmother.
teaching.audioText: She felt guilty because she had not called her grandmother.

teaching.en: He began to hesitate at the door, and his real motive was to say sorry.
teaching.es: Empezó a dudar ante la puerta, y su verdadero motivo era pedir perdón.
teaching.explanationEs: Hesitate es una acción que muestra el ánimo; motive es la razón que explica lo que hace.
segments: He began to hesitate at the door, and
his real motive was to say sorry.
teaching.audioText: He began to hesitate at the door, and his real motive was to say sorry.

teaching.en: She did not speak; she only continued to stare at the old photo.
teaching.es: No habló; solo siguió mirando fijamente la vieja foto.
teaching.explanationEs: Stare at es una acción sin palabras: el autor muestra el ánimo sin nombrarlo.
segments: She did not speak; she only continued
to stare at the old photo.
teaching.audioText: She did not speak; she only continued to stare at the old photo.

prompt.es: Elige qué siente Dani según lo que hace en el fragmento.

choices.text: He is calm and wants to go home.
He is proud of what he did.
He is anxious and unsure about going in.

feedback.es: Dani no se mueve y mira fijamente el picaporte: sus acciones muestran inquietud e inseguridad.

hint.es: Mira qué hace Dani: no se mueve y mira el picaporte.

origin.text: Outside the door, Dani waited for a long time. He stared at the handle and did not move. He wanted to say sorry to his sister, but every word seemed too small.

prompt.es: Elige el motivo de Dani para estar delante de la puerta.

choices.text: He wants to say sorry to his sister.
He wants to borrow something.
He is waiting for a friend.

feedback.es: El texto dice que quería pedir perdón a su hermana, pero las palabras le parecían pequeñas.

hint.es: Busca lo que Dani quería decirle a su hermana.

origin.text: Outside the door, Dani waited for a long time. He stared at the handle and did not move. He wanted to say sorry to his sister, but every word seemed too small.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo tiene muchas ganas de empezar, pero su hermana no.»

feedback.es: Eager expresa muchas ganas de hacer algo; contrasta con la actitud de la hermana.

origin.text: Leo is ___ to start, but his sister is not.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con el ánimo que transmite.

pairs: He hesitated at the door.
She looked away from him.
He smiled for the first time all day.
Her hands would not stop shaking.

feedback.es: Cada acción revela un ánimo: dudar muestra vacilación, apartar la vista evita, sonreír alivia y temblar delata nervios.

pairs: He hesitated at the door.
She looked away from him.
He smiled for the first time all day.
Her hands would not stop shaking.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige por qué Clara no contesta al teléfono.

choices.text: She is too busy with her homework.
She feels guilty about not visiting her grandmother.
She does not hear the phone.

feedback.es: Clara no contesta porque no ha visitado a su abuela desde hace semanas: el motivo es la culpa.

origin.audio: The phone rang, but Clara did not answer. She looked at the screen and put it face down on the table. It was her grandmother again, and she had not visited her for weeks.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se sintió aliviado cuando nadie lo vio.»

feedback.es: Relieved expresa el alivio de quien ya no tiene miedo a que lo descubran.

origin.text: He felt ___ when nobody saw him.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige cómo se siente Tom antes de hablar.

choices.text: He is proud of his speech.
He is tired of the lesson.
He is nervous about speaking.

feedback.es: Su corazón se hunde y se levanta despacio tras respirar hondo: son acciones de nerviosismo.

origin.audio: Tom had practised his speech all week. On Monday morning, his heart sank. When the teacher called his name, he took a deep breath and got up slowly. "I'm fine," he whispered to nobody.

prompt.es: Elige por qué Tom dice «I'm fine» en voz baja.

choices.text: He wants to hide that he is nervous.
He is really calm and happy.
He wants to leave the class.

feedback.es: Dice que está bien aunque sus acciones muestran miedo: quiere ocultar que está nervioso.

origin.text: Tom had practised his speech all week. On Monday morning, his heart sank. When the teacher called his name, he took a deep breath and got up slowly. "I'm fine," he whispered to nobody.

prompt.es: Elige qué quiere decir la expresión «his heart sank».

choices.text: He felt a pain and needed a doctor.
He felt a sudden worry inside.
He felt very happy and excited.

feedback.es: Heart sank es una expresión figurada: sentir de pronto preocupación o desánimo, no un dolor físico.

origin.text: Tom had practised his speech all week. On Monday morning, his heart sank. When the teacher called his name, he took a deep breath and got up slowly. "I'm fine," he whispered to nobody.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom parece reacio a levantarse: lo hace despacio.»

feedback.es: Reluctant describe a quien hace algo sin ganas; levantarse despacio lo muestra.

origin.text: Tom looks ___ to get up: he moves slowly.

prompt.es: Elige qué siente Nina al final del fragmento.

choices.text: She feels angry with her guests.
She feels afraid of the noise.
She feels proud of her cake.

feedback.es: Sonríe en silencio y se siente orgullosa: su gesto muestra satisfacción por lo que ha hecho.

origin.text: Nina looked at the cake she had made. Everyone was laughing and eating. She smiled quietly and felt very happy.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué muestra la duda de Sam.

choices.text: He starts to speak, stops, and says nothing important.
He speaks loudly and clearly.
He leaves the room at once.

feedback.es: Empezar a hablar, parar y no decir nada importante muestra que Sam duda si contar la verdad.

origin.audio: Sam wanted to tell his friend the truth. He started to speak, stopped, and looked at the floor. "It's nothing," he said.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ella evita hablar de aquel día.»

feedback.es: Avoid va seguido de -ing (talking): ella intenta no hablar de aquel día.

origin.text: She tries to ___ talking about that day.

es: Escribir una escena de recuerdo en primera persona con detalles sensoriales y verbos de memoria con gerundio o infinitivo (remember, forget, regret).

teaching.en: I remember playing on my grandmother's porch every summer.
teaching.es: Recuerdo haber jugado en el porche de mi abuela cada verano.
teaching.explanationEs: Remember + -ing es el recuerdo de algo que ya ocurrió: me veo jugando en el porche.
segments: I remember playing on my
grandmother's porch every summer.
teaching.audioText: I remember playing on my grandmother's porch every summer.

teaching.en: I must remember to call her on Sunday.
teaching.es: Tengo que acordarme de llamarla el domingo.
teaching.explanationEs: Remember + to es no olvidar una tarea futura: es una obligación, no un recuerdo.
segments: I must remember to
call her on Sunday.
teaching.audioText: I must remember to call her on Sunday.

teaching.en: I will never forget hearing the creak of that old gate.
teaching.es: Nunca olvidaré oír el chirrido de aquella vieja verja.
teaching.explanationEs: Forget + -ing es un recuerdo vivido que no se borra; creak añade un detalle de sonido.
segments: I will never forget hearing the
creak of that old gate.
teaching.audioText: I will never forget hearing the creak of that old gate.

teaching.en: I regret not saying goodbye to her.
teaching.es: Lamento no haberme despedido de ella.
teaching.explanationEs: Regret + -ing lamenta algo que hiciste o no hiciste; not va delante del -ing.
segments: I regret not saying
goodbye to her.
teaching.audioText: I regret not saying goodbye to her.

teaching.en: The scent of warm bread is a vivid memory for me.
teaching.es: El olor del pan caliente es para mí un recuerdo muy vívido.
teaching.explanationEs: Scent, warm y vivid son detalles de los sentidos: hacen que la escena se vea y se huela.
segments: The scent of warm bread is
a vivid memory for me.
teaching.audioText: The scent of warm bread is a vivid memory for me.

teaching.en: An echo of her voice still stays in my mind.
teaching.es: Un eco de su voz todavía permanece en mi mente.
teaching.explanationEs: Echo añade un detalle sonoro y lo une con la memoria: still marca que el recuerdo sigue ahí.
segments: An echo of her voice
still stays in my mind.
teaching.audioText: An echo of her voice still stays in my mind.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que recuerda algo ya ocurrido, no una tarea pendiente.

choices.text: I remember swimming in that lake as a child.
I must remember to swim in that lake.
I remember to swim in that lake as a child.

feedback.es: Remember + -ing recuerda algo vivido; las otras opciones son una tarea o una estructura incorrecta.

hint.es: Remember + -ing es el recuerdo de algo que viviste.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nunca olvidaré oír aquella canción en la radio.»

feedback.es: Forget + -ing expresa un recuerdo vivido que no se borra: hearing.

hint.es: Después de forget, para un recuerdo, va el verbo en -ing.

origin.text: I will never forget ___ that song on the radio.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me arrepiento de no haberle dicho la verdad.»

answer.text: I regret not telling him the truth

feedback.es: Regret va seguido de -ing y not se coloca antes: not telling.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con lo que significa.

pairs: I remember locking the door.
I must remember to lock the door.
I forgot to lock the door.
I regret locking the door.

feedback.es: La forma del verbo cambia el significado: -ing mira al pasado y to mira a una tarea.

pairs: I remember locking the door.
I must remember to lock the door.
I forgot to lock the door.
I regret locking the door.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sentido aparece en el recuerdo.

choices.text: The sense of sound.
The sense of smell.
The sense of touch.

feedback.es: Scent y smell son palabras del olfato: el recuerdo se apoya en el olor del pan.

origin.audio: I will never forget the scent of warm bread in my grandmother's kitchen. Every morning I woke up to that smell.

prompt.es: Completa: «Todavía oigo el eco de su risa.»

feedback.es: Echo añade un detalle de sonido al recuerdo: el eco de su risa.

origin.text: I can still hear the ___ of her laughing.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que expresa un recuerdo vivido del verano pasado.

choices.text: I remember to sit on the porch last summer.
I must remember sitting on the porch last summer.

prompt.es: Escribe la escena de recuerdo que se pide en el recuadro.

answer.text: I remember standing on my grandmother's porch on hot summer evenings. The air was warm, and the scent of fresh bread came from the kitchen. I can still hear the creak of the old gate and the echo of my cousins laughing in the garden. I will never forget watching the sun go down behind the hills while she told us stories. One evening, I forgot to say goodbye when my parents took me home, and I still regret not hugging her that night. Now I must remember to call her every Sunday. Sometimes I close my eyes, and that porch is there again, small and golden, exactly as it was. Some memories stay vivid for ever.
accepted: I remember standing on my grandmother's porch on hot summer evenings. The air was warm, and the scent of fresh bread came from the kitchen. I can still hear the creak of the old gate and the echo of my cousins laughing in the garden. I will never forget watching the sun go down behind the hills while she told us stories. One evening, I forgot to say goodbye when my parents took me home, and I still regret not hugging her that night. Now I must remember to call her every Sunday. Sometimes I close my eyes, and that porch is there again, small and golden, exactly as it was. Some memories stay vivid for ever.

I remember playing in my grandfather's garden every summer. The air was warm, and the scent of apples was everywhere. I can still hear the creak of the wooden gate and the echo of his voice calling us for dinner. I will never forget eating under the big tree while he told funny stories. I regret not asking him more questions about his life, and I must remember to visit his house again this year. When I close my eyes, that garden comes back, small and green and full of light. It is a vivid memory that I do not want to forget.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención en el club de lectura: resumen, recuerdo y respuesta.

answer.text: Thanks, Tom. I see your point, but I disagree. In this chapter, the plot turns when Mara finds the old letter in her aunt's kitchen, and she decides to read it alone. Although the ending is quiet, I found it very moving. I can relate to Mara, because I remember waiting for a letter from my grandmother every summer. I will never forget opening the envelope and seeing her small, careful writing. That memory makes the last scene feel true to me. Maybe the ending is not exciting, but it is honest. I also regret not keeping her letters, so perhaps that is why the chapter reminds me of her. What do you think?
